title: PAC file forwarding: limits, versions and what it cannot cover

prose.text: A PAC file points browsers at the service; how that traffic is treated once it arrives is in [[zia.proxy-mode.explicit]]. {{what-it-is}} {{benefits}}

prose.label: What it cannot do.
prose.text: {{limitations}} {{unknown-location-limits}} {{over-tunnel}} What PAC forwarding carries beyond HTTP and HTTPS is open {{gap:non-web-traffic}}, and client behavior under enforced authentication is open {{gap:auth-challenge-behavior}}. Authentication behavior is in [[zia.authentication.methods]] and [[zia.authentication.location-enforcement]].

prose.label: Hosting and changes.
prose.text: {{default-files}} {{limits}} {{version-states}} The request body of the version action differs across sources {{divergence:version-action-body}}. {{validation}} {{changes-immediate}} When clients pick up a changed file is open {{gap:client-cache}}, the default hosted URL is open {{gap:default-pac-url}}, and WPAD or MDM delivery is open {{gap:delivery-methods}}.

prose.label: Dedicated proxy ports.
prose.text: {{dedicated-port-variables}} The port service itself is in [[zia.forwarding-control.proxy-ports]].

prose.label: Automation.
prose.text: {{terraform-resource}} Creating a file may or may not deploy it {{divergence:create-vs-deploy}}, and the resulting state is open {{gap:pac-create-resulting-state}}. The Go response model and the Python and Automate shapes differ on `externalId` for the last-modifying admin {{go-lastmodifiedby-nullable}}; whether tenants populate it is open {{gap:pac-externalid-populated}}. The PAC file source is in [[shared.pac-files]].
Whether a location is required for PAC traffic is not stated (gap `location-not-required`); what the sources say about unknown sources is in [[zia.locations.model]].

what-it-is.statement: A PAC file is a text file that directs the browser to forward traffic to a Public Service Edge; it can exclude destinations (for example intranet sites) so they go direct, and it can be installed per user to cover them outside the corporate network.

quotes: A PAC file is a text file that directs the browser to forward traffic to a Public Service Edge.
Using PAC files allows you to set exceptions for forwarding your traffic, such as excluding intranet corporate sites from the Zscaler service.
You can install a PAC file for each of your users to ensure coverage outside the corporate network.

default-files.statement: Zscaler hosts four default PAC files (recommended.pac, proxy.pac, mobile_proxy.pac, kerberos.pac) that forward all browser traffic to the nearest Public Service Edge. They cannot be edited but can be copied into custom files, and the Kerberos file is recommended when Kerberos authentication is deployed.

quotes: The Zscaler service hosts 4 default PAC files: recommended.pac, proxy.pac, mobile_proxy.pac, and kerberos.pac.
The default PAC files are non-editable, but you can copy them to create and build your custom PAC files.
Zscaler recommends using the Kerberos PAC file if you are deploying Kerberos authentication.
These files are all configured to automatically forward all browser traffic to the nearest Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA).

limits.statement: By default an organization can have 256 PAC files (Support can raise this to 1,024), each up to 256 KB (Support can raise it to 2 MB), with up to 10 versions per file.

quotes: The number of PAC files allowed per organization is 256. Contact Zscaler Support to increase the limit of allowed PAC files to 1,024.
The size limit of each PAC file that you can upload is 256 KB. Contact Zscaler Support to increase the PAC file size limit to a maximum of 2 MB.
Zscaler allows you to host up to 10 versions of your custom PAC files at a time in the Zscaler Admin Console.

version-states.statement: A PAC version can be deployed, staged or marked last known good; only one version can be staged at a time and it is served from a different hosted URL than the deployed one, and deployed, staged or last-known-good versions cannot be deleted. The API actions are DEPLOY, STAGE, LKG, UNSTAGE and REMOVE_LKG.

quotes: You can stage only one PAC file version for deployment at a time, and the hosted URL for that PAC file is different from the deployed version.
The versions that are tagged as Deployed, Staged for Deployment, or Last Known Good cannot be deleted.

expect.description: Specifies the action that must be performed on the PAC file version

validation.statement: The console checks PAC syntax with Verify PAC File but still lets a file with errors be saved; the Python SDK validates content before it adds a file.

quotes: You can correct the PAC file and click Verify PAC File again to ensure that there are no errors, or you can save the PAC file with errors.
# Validate the PAC file content before proceeding

changes-immediate.statement: PAC file changes immediately affect the organization's traffic, so they should be verified and applied in a maintenance window, with a copy of the current file saved first. Staging serves a test version from its own hosted URL, different from the deployed version's, so users on the deployed URL do not receive it.

quotes: PAC file changes immediately impact your organization's traffic.
Zscaler highly recommends that you save a copy of your current PAC file before applying any changes.
Click Save & Deploy to deploy the PAC file with immediate effect.
If you're editing a PAC file, verify the changes and apply them during your organization's maintenance window.
You can create multiple versions for the same PAC file and can stage them for testing before deployment.
You can stage only one PAC file version for deployment at a time, and the hosted URL for that PAC file is different from the deployed version.

over-tunnel.statement: PAC-forwarded traffic that goes through a GRE or IPSec tunnel is subject to the tunnel's throughput limit. Government clouds support PAC files only when the proxy traffic is sent through a GRE or IPSec tunnel, not directly over the internet.

quotes: When PAC file-based traffic is forwarded through a GRE or IPSec tunnel, the throughput restriction of the tunnel applies.
Zscaler Government Clouds support PAC files only when the proxy traffic is sent through GRE or IPSec tunnels.

benefits.statement: PAC files are supported by all major browsers, protect users on and off the corporate network, can be enforced through Active Directory Group Policy for Internet Explorer settings, make exclusions easy, and allow a location when traffic comes from a static public IP; Surrogate IP can be used if the router can use XFF headers and that is enabled at the location.

quotes: All major browsers support PAC files.
Users on and off the corporate network are protected by the service.
Microsoft Internet Explorer PAC settings can be enforced organization-wide using Microsoft Active Directory Group Policies (GPO).
You can create locations if traffic is coming from a static public IP address.
If your router can use XFF headers, and it is enabled at your location, you can leverage the Surrogate IP feature.
If certain applications need to be excluded from the Zscaler service, it is easy to write an exclude statement in your PAC file to send traffic directly.

limitations.statement: PAC forwarding cannot use features that need a tunnel (Bandwidth Control and Firewall), covers only applications that support PAC files, can be bypassed by end users disabling the file, loses internal IP visibility and sublocation policy unless XFF headers are inserted (group and user policy still apply), and can affect SLAs and performance without GRE or IPSec.

quotes: You are not able to leverage some of the features of the Zscaler platform, such as Bandwidth Control and Firewall, because you need tunneling to use them.
End users can bypass the Zscaler service by disabling PAC files.
Unless XFF headers are inserted, Zscaler loses internal IP address visibility, and customers are not able to leverage the sublocation feature.
The service can apply group and user policies, but not sublocation policies.
SLAs and performance can be impacted if you don't implement GRE or IPSec tunnels.

evidence.after: A PAC file is a text file that directs the browser to forward traffic to a Public Service Edge.
quotes: Not all applications support PAC files, therefore not all traffic is secured by Zscaler.

unknown-location-limits.statement: When PAC-forwarded traffic arrives from an unknown location, features such as the firewall, sublocations and Surrogate IP are unavailable.

quotes: When user traffic is forwarded from unknown locations with a PAC file, some features of the Zscaler platform are unavailable, such as Firewall, sublocations, and Surrogate IP.
evidence.after: Using Tunneling, PAC Files, and Surrogate IP

dedicated-port-variables.statement: When PAC files send traffic to a dedicated proxy port, the file must use the ${GATEWAY_FX} and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY_FX} variables and not name specific Public Service Edges by host name or IP, so that failover and nearest-edge selection keep working.

quotes: Using PAC Files to Forward Traffic to a Dedicated Proxy Port
In this deployment, do not specify specific Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) by host names or IP addresses in the PAC file to prevent failover.
you must use the variables ${GATEWAY_FX} and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY_FX} to send web traffic to Public Service Edges closest to the user.

terraform-resource.statement: The Terraform provider has a zia_pac_files resource and data source.

quotes: "zia_pac_files": resourcePacFiles(),
"zia_pac_files": dataSourcePacFiles(),

go-lastmodifiedby-nullable.statement: Go v3.8.46 types the PAC file `lastModifiedBy` as a nullable pointer to the shared ID/name/extensions struct, which has no `externalId` member. The Python PAC model decodes `lastModifiedBy` through the shared `CommonBlocks`, which reads `externalId`, and the Automate response schema for the PAC list includes `externalId` on that object.

quotes: LastModifiedBy *common.IDNameExtensions `json:"lastModifiedBy,omitempty"`
type IDNameExtensions struct { ID int `json:"id,omitempty"` Name string `json:"name,omitempty"` Extensions map[string]interface{} `json:"extensions,omitempty"` }
self.external_id = config["externalId"] if "externalId" in config else False
self.last_modified_by = common.CommonBlocks(config["lastModifiedBy"])

default-pac-url.title: URL of the default hosted PAC file
default-pac-url.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZIA provides a hosted PAC file service at gateway.<cloud>.net/proxy.pac (the default PAC). No captured source states it; Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.

client-cache.title: When clients pick up a changed PAC file
client-cache.detail: Unverified legacy statement: PAC file changes take effect on the client's next PAC fetch cycle; browsers cache PAC files and the cache TTL varies by OS and browser, and a change takes minutes to about an hour to reach all users. Also open: the Cache-Control and Expires headers the Zscaler PAC servers send, whether a rollback reaches clients holding a cached newer version only after expiry, and any console action that forces a re-fetch. Settled for Client Connector's app profile PAC: it refreshes every 15 minutes and Update Policy syncs it at once (shared.pac-files.hosting:subcloud-propagation). A lab test (an HTTP HEAD on a hosted PAC URL) would settle the rest.

non-web-traffic.title: What PAC forwarding carries beyond HTTP and HTTPS
non-web-traffic.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Explicit proxying is TCP-only, with no UDP (RTP, QUIC, DNS-over-UDP) and no FTP, SSH or SMTP redirection. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.

auth-challenge-behavior.title: Client behavior when a PAC-forwarded location enforces authentication
auth-challenge-behavior.detail: Unverified legacy statement: With Enforce Authentication on, browsers get a 407; Kerberos and NTLM work transparently in IE and Edge on domain-joined Windows, Chrome and Firefox on non-domain-joined machines prompt interactively, and non-browser applications fail silently or loop on 407; deploying Client Connector removes the problem. Also open: whether a cookieless client gets a 407 or a SAML 302, how the session cookie is scoped across PAC-proxied requests, why users report more re-authentication in PAC mode than over Z-Tunnel, and what happens to a Kerberos-eligible user whose PAC file returns port 80 rather than 8800 (the Kerberos PAC file and port 8800 are in shared.pac-files.kerberos). No captured source states it; operator experience or a tenant observation would settle it.

delivery-methods.title: PAC delivery by WPAD, MDM and manual settings
delivery-methods.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The PAC file can be delivered by WPAD (a DNS record), by MDM profile or by manual proxy settings, and Chrome honors Internet Explorer settings on Windows. Also open: whether a Zscaler-hosted PAC can be served as wpad.dat or with the application/x-ns-proxy-autoconfig MIME type, whether DHCP option 252 can deliver the hosted URL, and whether a customer wpad host redirecting (HTTP 302) to the hosted URL keeps variable substitution. No captured source states it; operator experience or a tenant observation would settle it.

location-not-required.title: PAC traffic reaching ZIA with no configured Location
location-not-required.detail: Unverified legacy statement: PAC-forwarded traffic can reach ZIA without a pre-configured Location if it comes from a known-authenticated user, with reduced reporting granularity. No captured source states it; Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.

pac-externalid-populated.title: Whether current PAC responses populate externalId on lastModifiedBy
pac-externalid-populated.blocks: relying on externalId from a Go PAC read
pac-externalid-populated.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Go response model omits externalId while Python and the Automate schema retain it. The Go change is a response-model change and is not proof the service stopped returning the field.

quotes: LastModifiedBy *common.IDNameExtensions `json:"lastModifiedBy,omitempty"`

pac-create-resulting-state.title: Backend state of a newly created PAC file
pac-create-resulting-state.blocks: assuming a Terraform-created PAC file is, or is not, serving traffic
pac-create-resulting-state.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the provider and the captured Automate create text contradict each other on whether a created PAC file is already deployed. No live or acceptance result in the audited material shows the resulting state.

quotes: This request only adds a PAC file. The PAC file needs to be transitioned to the Deploy state in order for the file to be deployed.

version-action-body.summary: Request body of the PAC version action (DEPLOY, STAGE, LKG, UNSTAGE, REMOVE_LKG)

quotes: // serialized object corrupts the version's stored commit message.
serialized object corrupts the version's stored commit message.

positions.says: Go v3.8.46 sends the commit message as the raw request body and says serializing an object corrupts the stored commit message.

quotes: body.update(kwargs)

positions.says: Python builds a dictionary from the keyword fields (including pac_commit_message) and sends it as the JSON object body.

expect.operationId: Pac Resource Update Pac Version Flag

positions.says: The Automate operation takes the pacId, pacVersion, pacVersionAction path parameters and an optional newLKGVer query parameter, and declares no request body.

version-action-body.impact: Go callers pass only the commit message. The Go change is wrapper behavior, not a reproduced tenant test, so do not infer that Python fails or that the service accepts only one representation.

create-vs-deploy.summary: Whether creating a PAC file deploys it

quotes: // The service always deploys the initial version; surface a clear error
req.PACVersionStatus = "DEPLOYED"

positions.says: The provider says the service always deploys the initial version, rejects any pac_version_status other than DEPLOYED on create, and sends pacVersionStatus DEPLOYED in the create request.

quotes: This request only adds a PAC file. The PAC file needs to be transitioned to the Deploy state in order for the file to be deployed.

positions.says: The Automate create operation says it only adds a PAC file, which must be transitioned to the Deploy state to be deployed.

create-vs-deploy.impact: Whether a created PAC file is live (and affects traffic) immediately is not settled; the provider sentences are local validation and request facts, not proof of backend state.
